patterns.name: Classic Top Bar
patterns.whenToUse: Use when clarity, convention, or enterprise familiarity matters more than originality.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid as the default for creative, portfolio, artistic, or image-led pages where the nav should support a stronger composition.
patterns.visualBehavior: Logo or wordmark, primary links, and optional CTA arranged in a horizontal strip.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Can become crowded, low-contrast, or too small when compressed.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Collapse to bottom nav for app-like experiences with 3+ destinations, or a compact menu for scrolling-first websites.
patterns.migiNotes: Allowed when it earns clarity. Rejected when it is just navbar gravity.

patterns.name: Split Corner Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use for editorial, portfolio, or landing pages where the canvas needs breathing room and the nav can frame the composition.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when the product has many destinations or needs fast repeated switching.
patterns.visualBehavior: Identity in one corner with links, menu, or CTA distributed across other corners.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Spatial separation can hide relationships if labels are unclear.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Convert to compact menu plus primary CTA or bottom nav when app-like.
patterns.migiNotes: Good for making nav feel composed instead of pasted.

patterns.name: Centered Wordmark Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use when brand identity is the primary anchor and links can orbit or sit at edges.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid in dense tools where center space is needed for search, tabs, or status.
patterns.visualBehavior: Wordmark sits centrally while links are balanced around it or pushed to edges.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Can reduce scannability if the link order is unconventional.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Keep wordmark as page identity and move primary destinations to bottom nav or menu.
antiPatterns: centered logo with generic link row
patterns.migiNotes: Works when the wordmark is part of the page rhythm.

patterns.name: Editorial Header Strip
patterns.whenToUse: Use for portfolio, magazine, studio, or creative landing pages with minimal link needs.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when many destinations need persistent visibility.
patterns.visualBehavior: Thin, restrained header that reads like editorial metadata.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Small labels can lose contrast or touch size.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Preserve the editorial identity while moving deeper navigation into a menu.
patterns.migiNotes: Excellent when the page content carries the experience.

patterns.name: Oversized Typographic Menu
patterns.whenToUse: Use for bold portfolio, agency, experimental, or brand-world pages where navigation is a visual object.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid in productivity apps or pages where the menu would compete with task content.
patterns.visualBehavior: Menu labels or wordmark become large type and part of the hero composition.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Oversized type can crop, obscure hierarchy, or confuse link affordance.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Use a deliberate menu screen or compact high-character trigger.
antiPatterns: giant type with no readable interaction
patterns.migiNotes: High-character, but only when usability remains obvious.

patterns.name: Floating Contact Anchor
patterns.whenToUse: Use when contact/action is a primary business goal and can become a compositional anchor.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when it becomes a generic floating pill unrelated to the layout.
patterns.visualBehavior: CTA floats separately from the link system, often in a corner or edge.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Can overlap content or lose focus order if not planned.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Convert to sticky bottom action, bottom nav item, or safe-area aware floating button.
patterns.migiNotes: CTA placement should feel authored, not pasted.

patterns.name: Menu-First Minimal Nav
patterns.whenToUse: Use for cinematic, artistic, or focused pages where visible links would weaken the scene.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for task-heavy products where users need direct destination switching.
patterns.visualBehavior: Few visible links, often one strong menu trigger plus optional CTA.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Use a clear menu trigger with accessible expanded state.
antiPatterns: hamburger with no label in unfamiliar context
patterns.migiNotes: Minimal can be premium when the page itself carries orientation.

patterns.name: Spatial / Canvas Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use when a hero object, image, 3D stage, or immersive scene can hold links spatially.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid if links will become hard to find or collide with focal imagery.
patterns.visualBehavior: Nav items live around the scene or object rather than inside a conventional bar.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Spatial placement needs strong focus order and contrast.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Recompose into a compact menu or bottom nav while preserving the scene.
antiPatterns: random labels floating over busy imagery
patterns.migiNotes: One of the strongest ways to escape default navbar gravity.

patterns.name: Portfolio Index Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use for studios, creative portfolios, project galleries, or work-first sites.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for transactional products where project-index behavior is irrelevant.
patterns.visualBehavior: Work/About/Process/Contact or project links behave like part of an index or gallery system.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Index-like layouts need clear link grouping and keyboard order.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Convert to stacked index, compact menu, or bottom nav depending on destination count.
patterns.migiNotes: Makes navigation part of browsing, not chrome.

patterns.name: Vertical Side Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use for editorial layouts, dashboards, or staged pages where side labels support composition.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid when it wastes mobile space or creates cryptic rails.
patterns.visualBehavior: Small side rail, rotated labels, or vertical grouping along an edge.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Rotated text and icon-only rails can be hard to read.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Convert to bottom nav, compact tabs, or menu.
patterns.migiNotes: Useful only when it clarifies hierarchy or reinforces the page structure.

patterns.name: Bottom Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Default for mobile apps and mobile product flows with 3+ primary destinations.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for documentation sites, desktop-first enterprise tools, editor software, or scrolling-first websites unless justified.
patterns.visualBehavior: Primary destinations sit in a safe-area aware bottom bar or dock.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Can become cramped, generic, or unclear if icons and labels are weak.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Use generous touch targets, readable labels, intentional active state, and safe-area support.
patterns.migiNotes: The mobile default for app-like experiences.

patterns.name: Contextual Section Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use when section progression, story, or content state changes matter.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid if changing nav context will confuse users about available destinations.
patterns.visualBehavior: Nav highlights or adapts as the user moves through sections.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: State changes need clear semantics and keyboard support.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Use section progress, sticky context, or compact contextual controls.
patterns.migiNotes: Good for story-led pages when global orientation remains clear.

patterns.name: Floating Dock / Island Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use when a compact nav object fits the brand and does not fight the hero.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid as a default premium trope or when it obscures content.
patterns.visualBehavior: Small floating cluster with links, icons, or actions.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Needs focus ring, contrast, hit targets, and collision checks.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Convert to bottom nav or safe-area aware compact dock.
antiPatterns: sticky black bar with new colors
patterns.migiNotes: Only works when it feels intentional, not automatic.

patterns.name: Hidden / Progressive Navigation
patterns.whenToUse: Use for cinematic or highly focused landing experiences where primary action matters more than link browsing.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Avoid for content-heavy, ecommerce, dashboard, or app-like experiences.
patterns.visualBehavior: Global links are hidden behind a clear menu or revealed contextually.
patterns.accessibilityRisk: Discoverability and keyboard access must be protected.
patterns.mobileBehavior: Use an accessible menu drawer or progressive sheet.
antiPatterns: hidden links with no visible trigger
patterns.migiNotes: Useful when minimal nav lets the page become a scene.
